narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 63.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was denied.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Being in the bottom decile of your class that year, compared to an average around the middle of the pack among accepted students, signaled to the model that you would likely struggle with the exam. Your first-year class ranking was the second most important factor and also pulled the prediction toward failure; you placed in the second decile while accepted students averaged near the sixth.

Your undergraduate GPA was the third most influential feature, but it worked in the opposite direction. At 2.40 it is well below the 3.23 average of accepted students, yet the model still saw this as a modest positive signal relative to the rest of your profile.

Taken together, the model concluded that your relatively low class standings outweighed other information and made success on the bar exam uncertain enough to deny admission.

What you should do next is focus on strengthening your academic performance and consider retaking the LSAT or enrolling in a structured bar-preparation course before reapplying. Improving your class rank in future years and raising your GPA would directly address the factors that most hurt your application. (218 words)
